title: bench — the Netlib acceptance gate
summary: The Netlib acceptance gate: three instance sets, four per-instance predicates, and a per-instance baseline diff that decides whether a change passes.
scope: Netlib acceptance gate (M1 gate, PLAN 2.9)
standard set — 94 instances, each solved to a verified optimum, `make netlib`
Kennington set — 16 instances, same conditions, correctness only, `make netlib-kennington`
infeasible set — 29 instances, must classify INFEASIBLE, an instance returning `optimal` is flagged `<-- FALSE OPTIMUM` and fails the run, `make netlib-infeas`
gate predicate 1 — shape: the file must load with the row and column counts the manifest records (D18)
gate predicate 2 — objective: within `1e-6 · max(1, |reference|)` of the reference optimum, compared against reference plus `objconst` (PLAN 2.6)
gate predicate 3 — independent checker: primal feasibility, dual sign conditions, complementary slackness and the primal-dual gap, all judged in the original unscaled problem (D18)
gate predicate 4 — determinism: solved twice with the basis cleared between runs, agreeing on status, iteration count, work units, and the bits of the objective and every published value (D8, D68)
gate is all-or-nothing: reports NOT MET and `make netlib` exits non-zero unless every instance met every condition
baseline diff is the only regression detector once all three sets PASS; any predicate going from holding to not holding fails the run on its own, whatever the gate says
work growth allowed up to 2×, reported past that
`relative_suboptimality` carried in the baseline; growth past 2× above a floor of 1e-9 is a regression (D88, D91)
baseline update is a separate command (`make netlib-baseline` and per-set equivalents), never a side effect of running the gate
a run that compared against no baseline records `baseline: NOT COMPARED`
no wall-clock figure is produced by the gate; speed is an M2 question (D17)
`J=N` parallel runs produce a byte-identical record but invalidate the seconds; the time ratio a change is judged on (D45) must come from `J=1` (D57)
record columns that judge nothing: `rowrel`, `Q`, `N`, `drop`, `cert`, `rsub`, `sub`, `rays` (D24, D73, D91)
reference optima taken from Koch, *The Final NETLIB-LP Results* (ZIB-Report 03-05), every manifest line sourced `koch`
netlib's `emps` used as a dev-time expander, pinned by sha256 and never stored in the repo (PLAN Q6)
instance files never enter the repository; the manifest stands in for them (PLAN 2.10)

`make warm` / `make warm-kennington` — warm vs cold ratios after one branch-and-bound branching step; reports a ratio, not a verdict; fails on verdict/objective disagreement or checker refusal of either answer (D46, D69, D92)
bench/fetch.sh, run.c, bench/warm.c, the three manifests, the three baselines, results/
notes: Type taken from MANIFEST_TYPE (DOC), heuristic and content classification skipped. Content signals would independently read DOC: prose-heavy, no frontmatter, no Decision/Consequences pair, no user stories. Two resolved ambiguities. (1) The doc is typed DOC but its gate criteria are hard constraints on any future work, not background — the four per-instance predicates, the all-or-nothing rule, the baseline-diff regression rules and the J=1 requirement for time ratios are recorded in scope verbatim so a low-precedence type does not lose them. (2) DECISIONS.md is not named in the text; it is entered in cross_refs because the doc cites it 13 times by decision ID (D8, D17, D18, D24, D45, D46, D57, D68, D69, D73, D82, D88, D91, D92), which is this project's citation convention. PLAN.md likewise cited as 'PLAN 2.6', 'PLAN 2.9', 'PLAN 2.10', 'PLAN Q6', 'PLAN Q8'. Filename deviates from the {slug}-{sha256[0:8]} convention: no shell or hashing tool is available to this agent, so the repo-relative path slug 'bench-README' is used instead — it is unique across the three README.md entries in the ingest manifest (bench/README.md, bench/compare/README.md, README.md), which is what the hash suffix existed to guarantee.
